Approval is one step. This ledger follows funding into budgets, awards, and actual expenditures, keeping each stage distinct.

::: {.callout-note title="Reading the spending ledger"}
The ledger contains only sourced financial records. The original guide’s borrowing amounts describe proposed authorizations; they are not evidence of debt issued, money spent, or projects delivered. An empty ledger does not establish that no spending occurred.
:::

## Spending ledger

```{r}
#| results: asis
source("R/publication.R")
spending_table()
```

## What will be recorded

Each record will identify its measure, project, financial stage, funding source, responsible agency, date, amount, and supporting document. Where records allow, it will also describe the project location, intended service area, and beneficiaries.

**A project’s address is not the full geography of its benefits.** A school, library, housing program, or water project may serve residents beyond the neighborhood where it is located. Citywide and unlocated funding will remain visible without a made-up map point.

## Follow the stages

| Stage | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| Authorized | Permission or a limit established by the governing action |
| Budgeted | Funding allocated through the budget |
| Awarded | A documented grant, contract, or other award |
| Expended | An actual payment or expenditure recorded |

These stages are not additive. The same dollar may appear at successive stages. Records must also establish a link to the ballot measure; general spending on the same topic is not automatically attributable to it.
